summary: Created an SSH host CA on node1, signed the ed25519 host key with it, configured sshd to present the certificate, and verified a client trusting only the CA (no pinned host key) connects successfully with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes. Falsified by showing the same client fails without CA trust. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, rebooted node1 via shutdown -r now, confirmed boot_id changed after reconnect, and re-verified sshd health, the host certificate, and CA-trust client connectivity post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected existing SSH host keys, sshd_config, and OpenSSH 7.4 support for certificates on node1
Generated an ed25519 SSH CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca on node1
Signed the node's ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub as a host certificate (-h) with principals node1,10.100.93.10, producing /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub
Added HostCertificate /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub to /etc/ssh/sshd_config, validated with sshd -t, and reloaded sshd
Added CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY to the antrieb user's authorized_keys to enable a client-side SSH test
Verified a client with only @cert-authority trust for the CA (no pinned host key) connects under StrictHostKeyChecking=yes
Falsified the result by showing the same client fails host key verification without the CA trust line
Cleaned up temporary client key/known_hosts files
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service/cert health baseline
Rebooted node1 with shutdown -r now (acknowledgement returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until reachable again and confirmed boot_id changed
Re-verified sshd active, certificate intact, sshd_config setting present, and CA-trust client connection succeeding post-restart

evidence.summary: Generated ed25519 CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_host_ca with fingerprint SHA256:FDxAqqRfoJsRTqDdLglWTUvXfIkbNkve7fJVCKJleDo

evidence.requirement: Host key signed by CA as a host certificate
evidence.summary: ssh-keygen -s signed ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub with -h, principals node1 and 10.100.93.10, producing ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub verified via ssh-keygen -Lf

evidence.requirement: sshd configured to present the certificate
evidence.summary: Added HostCertificate directive to sshd_config, passed sshd -t syntax check, reloaded sshd (active)

evidence.requirement: Client connects trusting only the CA, without pinning the host key
evidence.summary: Authorized cluster key for test access, built known_hosts containing only an @cert-authority line for the CA, then ssh with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes succeeded (CLIENT_CONNECTED_VIA_CA)

evidence.requirement: Falsification: CA trust is what enables the connection
evidence.summary: Same client with an empty known_hosts (no CA trust) failed with 'Host key verification failed', proving the CA certificate is what permits the earlier success
Captured boot_id 73bafeef-b823-49b3-8e3d-17981e865b31, sshd active, host certificate present
shutdown -r now launched via backgrounded nohup; REBOOT_ACK returned before the connection dropped

evidence.requirement: Node unreachable during restart then boot identity changed (node1)
evidence.summary: Polling showed connection timeouts during reboot, then boot_id changed to 15ef0089-449e-4221-a79a-29cce8418c0e, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services and certificate (node1)
evidence.summary: sshd active, host certificate still present at /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub, HostCertificate directive intact in sshd_config

evidence.requirement: Post-restart proof the CA-based trust still functions (node1)
evidence.summary: Client trusting only the CA (no pinned host key) reconnected successfully after reboot (POST_RESTART_CA_TRUST_OK)
